name: AD8606ARZ
title: AD8605/AD8606/AD8608: single, dual and quad CMOS op amps, precision and low noise, inputs and outputs rail to rail
summary: Single (AD8605), dual (AD8606) and quad (AD8608) precision CMOS operational amplifiers with rail-to-rail inputs and outputs, running from one 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply. Offset is at most 65 µV (AD8605/AD8606, VS = 3.5 V), input bias current at most 1 pA, voltage noise 8 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz and gain-bandwidth 10 MHz, with no phase reversal. AD8606ARZ is the dual in an 8-lead narrow SOIC.

circuits.title: Snubber Network Configuration
circuits.description: Amplifier A of the AD8606 runs as a unity-gain follower driving a large capacitive load CL in parallel with RL. A series RS-CS network from the output to ground damps the ringing the capacitance would otherwise cause, without lowering the output swing; it does not give back the bandwidth the load costs. With CL = 1000 pF, RS = 90 Ω and CS = 700 pF bring the step overshoot from above 70 % to under 5 %.
notes: Supply pin numbers marked 4 (V+) and 8 (V−) should read 8 (V+) and 4 (V−).
RS = 90 Ω and CS = 700 pF are the pair used for the 1000 pF step response at VS = ±2.5 V.

circuits.title: Equivalent Circuit for Photodiode Preamp
circuits.description: A transimpedance stage: the photodiode, drawn as its photocurrent ID in parallel with its shunt resistance RD and capacitance CD, feeds the inverting input while the noninverting input is grounded. RF = 10 MΩ turns the current into the output voltage and CF = 10 pF sits across it. Output error is the offset gained up by (1 + RF/RD) plus RF times the bias current: about 100 µV at room temperature, rising to roughly 1 mV at 85 °C.

parts.note: current source, arrow pointing from the input node to ground

notes: VOS, in series with the inverting input, stands for the amplifier offset; it is not a component.

circuits.title: Single-Supply Headphone/Speaker Amplifier
circuits.description: Both halves of an AD8606 on one 5 V supply drive the two sides of a headphone. Each input is AC-coupled through 1 µF into a 20 kΩ/20 kΩ divider that holds the noninverting input at half the supply; the coupling cap and the divider form a high-pass at 1/[2π(R1||R2)C1]. Each half is a unity-gain follower whose output reaches the earpiece through 100 µF and 20 Ω, with 1 kΩ to ground after the coupling capacitor. Into a 16 Ω headphone THD + N stays near −60 dB across the audio band.

circuits.title: Difference Amplifier, AV = 10
circuits.description: A single AD8605 on 5 V subtracts V1 from V2 with a gain of 10: 1 kΩ input resistors and 10 kΩ feedback and ground-leg resistors, so VOUT = (R2/R1)(V2 − V1) when R4/R3 = R2/R1. With resistors matched to 0.01 % the common-mode rejection is 74 dB and the gain error is smallest.

circuits.title: Bipolar Operation
circuits.description: A current-output DAC (AD7545) with an AD8606 in two stages gives a bipolar output. Amplifier A is the first stage, a buffer at the DAC output: its inverting input takes OUT1 and its output returns to the DAC's RFB pin through RCS. C1 = 33 pF from OUT1 to that output forms a low-pass with the DAC's output resistance Req and so adds phase lead to compensate the frequency response. Amplifier B is the gain stage: its inverting input sums the first stage through R1 = 10 kΩ and VIN through R3 = 20 kΩ, with R2 = 10 kΩ feedback. Both noninverting inputs return to ground (B through R4 = 5 kΩ) to cut common-mode error; matching R1, R2 and R3 to 0.01 % gives 74 dB CMRR and the least gain error.

notes: AD7545 pin numbers: VDD 18, RFB 20, VREF 19, OUT1 1, AGND 2, DB11 4.

operation.text: AD8605 (single), AD8606 (dual) and AD8608 (quad) are CMOS op amps whose inputs and outputs both swing rail to rail on a single 2.7 V to 5.5 V supply. Offset is trimmed with ADI's DigiTrim method rather than by laser. They are unity-gain stable and specified from −40 °C to +125 °C.

Named applications: photodiode amplifiers, battery-powered and loop-powered instruments, multipole filters, integrators, sensors and high-impedance sensors, barcode scanners, optical control loops and audio in portable devices.
The output keeps its polarity even when the input is driven more than 2 V beyond the supply; it clamps at the rail rather than flipping.

Internal protection is present, but an input taken more than 0.5 V outside the supplies needs a series resistor that holds the input current to 5 mA. Because the offset current is below 1 pA, large resistors are acceptable: 10 kΩ adds under 10 nV of output error and the resistor's own thermal noise stays below 13 nV/√Hz at room temperature.
Each kΩ in the source adds less than 0.5 nV of input offset at room temperature, and up to 10 nV at 85 °C.
In unity gain (the worst case) with a 10 kΩ load, THD + N of the AD8605 stays below 0.005 % (−86 dB) over the whole audio band.
Between the two AD8606 amplifiers the separation exceeds 160 dB up to 1 MHz.

In unity gain the part drives 1000 pF without oscillating. Larger loads may need help: an RC snubber from output to ground cuts overshoot and ringing without reducing swing, or a resistor of about 100 Ω in series with the output inside the feedback loop does the same at the cost of some swing.

The bare-die WLCSP (AD8605ACB) sits bump side down, so light reflected from the board reaches the active silicon. Only input bias current changes: none at 0.1 mW/cm² office lighting, but up to 4500 pA at 3 mW/cm² and 850 nm. Sensitivity is highest in the near infrared (700 nm to 1000 nm); beyond 1100 nm silicon is transparent and there is no effect, and light on the back (substrate) face does nothing. The under-bump metal shields the most sensitive areas; where light is still a problem, covering the bump side with an opaque underfill such as silica-filled liquid epoxy removes it.

Buffering a current-output DAC, the feedback resistor converts its current to a voltage. The DAC's output resistance and capacitance both vary with code; a 10 pF to 30 pF capacitor across the feedback resistor offsets the pole of the DAC capacitance and can be trimmed for best response.
